title: Beef Bulgogi
subtitle: sweet-soy marinated beef, grilled or pan-fried
excerpt: Bulgogi is one of Korea's most beloved dishes -- thinly sliced beef marinated in soy, pear, and garlic, then cooked over high heat until caramelised. The pear tenderises the meat and adds a gentle sweetness. It is fast enough for a weeknight but flavourful enough for a weekend table.
sourceNotes: Bulgogi (literally fire meat) has roots in ancient Korean cuisine. References appear in records from the Goguryeo kingdom (37 BC -- 668 AD). The modern version with soy sauce and sugar developed in the twentieth century and is now one of the most internationally recognised Korean dishes.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The beef can marinate in the fridge for up to 4 hours before cooking.

content.text: Bulgogi means fire meat in Korean. Thinly sliced beef is soaked in a sweet, garlicky marinade and then cooked over very high heat until the edges caramelise. Freeze the beef for 30 minutes before slicing -- this firms it up and makes thin slices much easier to cut.

items.prepNote: sliced as thin as possible -- freeze for 30 minutes to make slicing easier
use 1 grated Asian pear or regular pear for the marinade -- the acid tenderises the beef
use toasted sesame oil -- add to the marinade

content.text: Mix the soy sauce, pear (or vinegar), honey, brown sugar, garlic, ginger, and sesame oil in a bowl.
Add the sliced beef and toss to coat. Marinate for at least 30 minutes at room temperature, or up to 4 hours in the fridge.
Heat a frying pan or griddle over the highest heat possible. Do not add oil -- the marinade contains enough.
Cook the beef in batches -- do not crowd the pan. Each batch should take about 2 minutes. The beef should caramelise at the edges.
Serve immediately on a bed of steamed rice with spring onion scattered over. Wrap in lettuce leaves if you like.

items.symptom: Beef is stewing rather than caramelising
items.cause: Pan not hot enough or too much beef in the pan at once
items.fix: The pan must be screaming hot before the beef goes in. Cook in small batches -- too much meat lowers the temperature and the beef steams rather than sears.

content.text: Bulgogi is Korean home cooking at its most satisfying. It is cooked at the table on gas grills in Korean barbecue restaurants. At home, a hot frying pan or griddle gives excellent results. The sweet, caramelised flavour is hard to resist. It is often served with rice, kimchi, and lettuce for wrapping.
